PAPERS.title: Exposure to Fine Particulate Matter During Pregnancy and Postpartum Psychological Functioning in the ECHO Cohort: Effect Modification by Body Mass Index.
PAPERS.short: ECHO 18-site US pregnancy PM2.5 postpartum EPDS anhedonia BMI effect modification DLM
PAPERS.pm: Daily residential PM2.5 from a validated satellite-based spatiotemporal hybrid model over the pregnancy residential history
PAPERS.endpoint: Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale total, anhedonia and depressive subscales within 1 y of delivery
PAPERS.affil: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, USA; not stated in record
PAPERS.n: 6,407 pregnant women from 18 ECHO sites; residential PM2.5 from a satellite-based hybrid model, EPDS completed within a year of delivery, analysed with GAMs, distributed lag models and trimester windows. Main-effect models found no overall PM2.5-EPDS association. Thin-plate GAMs suggested a nonlinear PM2.5 x pre-pregnancy BMI interaction for the anhedonia subscale (interaction p=0.06), with positive associations at higher BMI, strongest for first-trimester exposure; DLM cumulative estimates agreed. No effect sizes or CIs are given in the abstract. The headline is a borderline interaction from a two-dimensional smooth after a null main effect, with multiple windows and three outcomes, so it is hypothesis-generating at best. Relevance: indirect - modelled exposure with no measurement contribution; susceptibility-by-BMI framing could inform targeted personal monitoring.

PAPERS.title: Cardiac Rhythm Disorders and Chronic Occupational Exposure to Pollutants: A Systematic Review.
PAPERS.short: Toulouse systematic review occupational pollutants arrhythmia atrial fibrillation lead CS2 solvents inhalable particles
PAPERS.pm: Occupational inhalable particles among metals, solvents, gases and pesticides; exposure metrics as reported by 21 primary studies
PAPERS.affil: Toulouse-Purpan University Hospital, France; Toulouse-Purpan University Hospital, France
PAPERS.n: Systematic review of 21 studies on chronic occupational exposure (metals, solvents, aldehydes, amines, cyanides, plastics, acids, gases, pesticides) and cardiac arrhythmia. Lead, carbon disulfide, certain solvents and inhalable particles were associated with arrhythmias, chiefly atrial fibrillation; oxidative stress, cytotoxicity and inflammation are proposed as mechanisms. No pooled estimate, risk-of-bias grading or particle size fraction is reported in the abstract, so the particle signal cannot be separated from co-exposures in the source workplaces. Metadata gives no search dates or databases beyond 'several'. Relevance: low - occupational particle exposure is mentioned but not quantified; wearable PM monitoring in factories is the obvious missing exposure layer.

PAPERS.title: Indoor Air Quality Management for Patients with COPD and IPF: Practical Recommendations Based on Current Standards and Evidence.
PAPERS.short: Korea narrative review indoor air quality management COPD IPF nine-parameter action references
PAPERS.pm: Indoor PM2.5 and PM10 alongside NO2, CO2, formaldehyde, TVOC, CO, O3 and relative humidity; reference values from national and international standards
PAPERS.endpoint: Practical IAQ action references and maintenance targets for COPD and IPF patients
PAPERS.affil: Yonsei University, Republic of Korea; Yonsei University College of Medicine, Republic of Korea
PAPERS.n: Focused narrative review proposing residential indoor air quality management rules for patients with COPD and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. Nine parameters were selected (PM2.5, PM10, NO2, CO2, formaldehyde, TVOC, CO, O3, relative humidity), each with an action reference and a maintenance target that keep the source standard's averaging time; ambient forecast categories are used only for outdoor-driven pollutants. Recommendations: source control, forecast-guided ventilation, particle filtration and cooking/combustion control. The thresholds are explicitly not disease-specific clinical cut-offs, and no new exposure-response evidence is presented. Relevance: moderate - the framework presumes a home monitor reporting PM2.5 and PM10 at standard averaging times, exactly the use case for consumer-grade sensors, whose bias at high humidity is not addressed.

PAPERS.title: Mortality and Health Losses From Diseases Attributable to Air Pollution in Ethiopia, From 1990 to 2023.
PAPERS.short: GBD 2023 Ethiopia national subnational air pollution deaths DALYs ambient PM household solid fuel 1990-2023
PAPERS.pm: GBD 2023 ambient PM2.5 and household air pollution from solid fuels exposure estimates
PAPERS.endpoint: Deaths, YLDs, YLLs and DALYs attributable to air pollution
PAPERS.affil: Adigrat University, Ethiopia; Bule Hora University, Ethiopia
PAPERS.n: GBD 2023 secondary analysis for Ethiopia, national and subnational, 1990-2023. In 2023 air pollution was attributed 139 deaths per 100,000 (95% UI 106-177), 4,286 YLLs (3,475-5,107) and 4,557 DALYs per 100,000 (3,685-5,397); YLDs were driven by household solid fuels (247 per 100,000, UI 152-344). Addis Ababa had the highest ambient PM mortality (64 per 100,000, UI 43-88) and the lowest household air pollution mortality; Afar had the highest overall mortality (185, UI 137-232). Mortality rates were flat across 33 years while DALY rates fell. Every number inherits GBD's exposure surface, which in Ethiopia rests on very few ground monitors; the subnational contrasts are model outputs, not observations. Relevance: high in principle - Ethiopia is a textbook case where a low-cost network would constrain the ambient surface the burden depends on.

PAPERS.title: Monitoring and modelling of indoor environmental quality to guide indoor greening applications.
PAPERS.short: GCARE review 60 studies indoor green infrastructure IEQ monitoring modelling VOC PM removal
PAPERS.pm: Indoor PM and VOCs with temperature, humidity and CO2 as monitored in 60 indoor-greening studies
PAPERS.endpoint: Indoor environmental quality change attributable to indoor green infrastructure
PAPERS.affil: University of Surrey (GCARE), United Kingdom; Federal Institute of Hydrology, Germany
PAPERS.n: Review of 60 studies of passive (potted plants, green walls, indoor trees) and active (hydroponics, biofilters) indoor greening and indoor environmental quality. Passive systems typically cut VOCs 10-30% and buffer temperature and humidity; active systems removed VOCs and PM more efficiently. 59% of studies were laboratory, 33% in situ, many with 6-48 h chamber runs; controlled settings overstate removal relative to real buildings, and descriptors and ventilation data are not standardised. Passive configurations reduced cooling demand 22-27%. No PM removal rate is quantified in the abstract, and the evidence is dominated by short chamber tests with few taxa. Relevance: moderate - the review's main ask, long in-situ IEQ monitoring with ventilation logging, is a direct job for indoor low-cost PM/CO2 nodes.

PAPERS.title: First observations of aerosol mass fluxes over open water using a large-aperture scintillometer
PAPERS.short: Eastern China lake and coastal bay large-aperture scintillometer aerosol mass flux RMN(RH) PM10 calibration
PAPERS.pm: Path-averaged aerosol mass flux from large-aperture scintillometer log-intensity spectra; conversion factor calibrated against PM10, visibility and RH
PAPERS.geo: China (eastern; inland lake and coastal bay)
PAPERS.endpoint: Aerosol mass-flux magnitude over open water
PAPERS.n: First large-aperture scintillometer (LAS) retrieval of path-averaged aerosol mass flux over open water, four campaigns at an inland lake and a coastal bay in eastern China. The aerosol (imaginary) and thermodynamic (real) refractive-index contributions were separated from the log-intensity spectrum, and the constant mass-to-optical conversion factor was replaced by a campaign-specific RMN(RH) calibrated against PM10, visibility and RH; RMN fell consistently with humidity. Campaign-median flux magnitudes were 0.091-0.399 ug m-2 s-1, with daytime enhancement; dense coastal fog was the main operational limit. Magnitudes only (no sign), validation is against calculated dry deposition rather than eddy covariance, and n=4 campaigns. Relevance: moderate - the RH-dependent optical-to-mass conversion is the same hygroscopic problem that biases optical low-cost PM sensors.

PAPERS.title: Vertically stratified long-range transport of biomass-burning aerosol over Reunion Island during September 2017
PAPERS.short: Reunion Island September 2017 biomass-burning aerosol layers lidar AERONET FTIR CO CAMS FLEXPART
PAPERS.pm: AERONET AOD 550 nm, Raman/elastic lidar layers, CALIOP, MODIS, CAMS EAC4 reanalysis; FLEXPART source attribution
PAPERS.endpoint: Vertical structure and source of free-tropospheric smoke layers
PAPERS.n: Case study of a September 2017 biomass-burning aerosol episode over Reunion Island combining AERONET, ground lidar, FTIR CO, MODIS, CALIOP, CAMS EAC4 and FLEXPART. AOD at 550 nm reached 0.16-0.42. Lidar resolved one layer at 2.8-4.7 km on 19 September (Angstrom 355/532 = 1.32 +/- 0.23) and two on 25 September: 3.3-5 km (1.45 +/- 0.12) and a drier 5-9 km layer (1.60 +/- 0.06). FLEXPART, checked against smoothed FTIR CO, attributes both to southern Africa with a South American contribution to the lower layer. Two days in one month; layers sit in the free troposphere, so surface PM implications are not addressed. Relevance: low - column/vertical context only; a reminder that column AOD in satellite-fusion models can be decoupled from surface PM.

PAPERS.title: Meteorological conditions and aerosol-meteorology feedback drive divergent responses of co-occurring PM 2.5 and O 3 pollution to NO x -VOC perturbations in Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei-Shandong
PAPERS.short: BTHS July 2020 WRF-Chem double-high PM2.5 O3 NOx-VOC perturbation meteorological regimes aerosol feedback
PAPERS.pm: WRF-Chem simulated PM2.5 and O3 under joint NOx-VOC emission perturbations, five meteorological regimes
PAPERS.endpoint: Modelled PM2.5 and O3 response to precursor reductions
PAPERS.n: WRF-Chem for July 2020 over Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei-Shandong, classifying co-occurring PM2.5/O3 'double high' days into five regimes by boundary-layer height, temperature and humidity. PM2.5 was highest under Stable and WarmHumid (~46 ug/m3) and lowest under DryHot (~40); O3 highest under DryHot and Moderate (~163 ug/m3). At 50%/50% NOx/VOC cuts, PM2.5 fell 20.6% (Stable) and 20.9% (WarmHumid) but only 15.2% (DryHot); O3 fell 25.2% (WarmHumid) and 23.3% (DryHot). Aerosol-meteorology feedback amplified PM2.5 reductions in the Stable and WarmHumid regimes. One month, one model, no reported evaluation statistics in the abstract. Relevance: low-moderate - regime-dependent control efficacy is testable with dense sensor networks resolving boundary-layer-driven PM variability.

PAPERS.title: Geo-environmental controls on primordial radionuclides in air-conditioner filter dust: Source appraisals and dose-based assessment
PAPERS.short: Air-conditioner filter dust primordial radionuclides geo-environmental controls dose assessment
PAPERS.pm: Metadata only - indoor air-conditioner filter dust as a settled-particle sampler
PAPERS.endpoint: Metadata only - radionuclide activity and dose estimates
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: no abstract was retrievable from PubMed, Europe PMC or Crossref. The record (Atmospheric Pollution Research; Abedin, Rahman, Khan) uses air-conditioner filter dust to appraise primordial radionuclide sources and dose. No finding is asserted here. Relevance: indirect - HVAC filters as passive integrating particle samplers are a known complement to real-time indoor PM sensors.

PAPERS.title: Calibration of a Low-Cost Particulate Matter Sensor Using the Growing Factor
PAPERS.short: Low-cost PM sensor calibration hygroscopic growth factor Hungary AAQR
PAPERS.pm: Metadata only - low-cost optical PM sensor corrected with a hygroscopic growth factor
PAPERS.endpoint: Metadata only - calibrated low-cost PM against reference
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: no abstract was retrievable from Crossref or the harvest legs. The title states a calibration of a low-cost particulate matter sensor using the hygroscopic growth factor (Aerosol and Air Quality Research; Kiss, Kiss, Veres). No finding, sensor model or error metric is asserted here. Relevance: high - kappa-Kohler/growth-factor humidity correction is the physics-based alternative to purely empirical RH terms in LCS calibration; worth pulling the full text for R2/RMSE and sensor model.

PAPERS.title: Long-term spatiotemporal trends and regional disparities in aerosol optical depth across Koppen climatic regions of India
PAPERS.short: India AOD long-term trends Koppen climate regions regional disparities
PAPERS.pm: Metadata only - satellite aerosol optical depth trends
PAPERS.endpoint: Metadata only - AOD spatiotemporal trends by Koppen region
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: no abstract was retrievable. The record (Atmospheric Research; Tiwari, Gupta, Singh) analyses long-term AOD trends and regional disparities across Koppen climatic regions of India. No finding is asserted here. Relevance: indirect - stratifying AOD by climate regime is relevant to how AOD-to-PM2.5 conversion should vary in satellite-fusion models.

PAPERS.title: Identification of mineral microparticles accumulated in equine lung tissue: Is there a link between the environment and the development of interstitial lung disease? A case-control study.
PAPERS.short: Lyon equine fibrosing ILD SEM/EDS lung mineral microparticles case-control geogenic anthropogenic steel
PAPERS.pm: SEM/EDS count and classification of mineral microparticles in lung tissue; owner questionnaire for environment
PAPERS.affil: VetAgro Sup, University of Lyon, France; VetAgro Sup, University of Lyon, France
PAPERS.n: Case-control study of lung tissue from 21 equids with fibrosing interstitial lung disease and 10 healthy horses, particles counted and classified by SEM/EDS. Geogenic particles dominated all samples. Anthropogenic particle share was higher in idiopathic cases (median 20.2%, IQR 4.9-66.7) than controls (2.3%, 1.3-4.5; p=0.032); FeCrNi steel particles were more common in cases, and calcium compounds and iron oxide occurred only in idiopathic cases. Steel and iron-oxide proportions correlated with living indoors (R2 0.26 and 0.48). Questionnaire exposures did not differ. Ten controls, retrospective blocks, and no air measurements, so source attribution is inferential. Relevance: low - stable/barn particle exposure in a sentinel species; no sensing content.

PAPERS.title: The impact of ambient and wildfire-specific air pollution on upper airway disease.
PAPERS.short: UCSF MGB review ambient and wildfire air pollution chronic rhinosinusitis olfaction allergic rhinitis head and neck cancer
PAPERS.pm: Ambient air pollution and wildfire-specific air pollution as characterised in the reviewed studies
PAPERS.endpoint: Chronic rhinosinusitis, olfactory dysfunction, allergic rhinitis, head and neck cancer
PAPERS.affil: University of California San Francisco, USA; Mass General Brigham, USA
PAPERS.n: Narrative review of ambient and wildfire-specific air pollution and upper airway disease. Recent biobank and claims studies strengthen ambient associations with allergic rhinitis and chronic rhinosinusitis incidence, with emerging evidence that pollution shapes inflammatory endotype and blunts symptom improvement after endoscopic sinus surgery; wildfire smoke shows a dose-dependent association with acute rhinosinusitis care and with head and neck cancer incidence. No new estimates; the abstract gives no effect sizes, and the cited wildfire metrics are mostly modelled smoke PM2.5. Relevance: indirect - the call for prospective mechanistic studies would benefit from personal or home PM2.5 during smoke events.

PAPERS.title: Air Pollution and Cancer Research Worldwide: Citation Dynamics, Emerging Trends, and Collaborative Networks.
PAPERS.short: Scopus 2020-2025 scientometric air pollution and cancer 3056 documents collaboration networks
PAPERS.endpoint: Scholarly output, citation impact, collaboration and thematic evolution
PAPERS.affil: Universidad Nacional Federico Villarreal, Peru; Universidad San Ignacio de Loyola, Peru
PAPERS.n: Scientometric analysis of 3,056 Scopus documents (1,401 sources) on air pollution and cancer published 2020-2025, using SciVal and Bibliometrix: output growth (13.3% per year), CiteScore, SNIP, h-index, Bradford core journals, collaboration life-cycle and thematic evolution. The abstract does not report the leading themes, countries or networks in quantitative form. Bibliometrics counts papers, not evidence; it says nothing about effect sizes or exposure quality. Relevance: low - no exposure or measurement content.

PAPERS.title: Poorer Air Quality During Trimesters 2 and 3 of Gestation Is Associated With Decreased Bone Mineral Density in Childhood and Adolescence.
PAPERS.short: New Mexico 597 paediatric decedents postmortem CT bone mineral density gestational AQI trimester
PAPERS.pm: County-level Air Quality Index over the 9 months before birth, by trimester; ambient temperature extremes
PAPERS.endpoint: Bone mineral density and porous cranial lesions on postmortem CT
PAPERS.affil: University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center, USA; University of New Mexico, USA
PAPERS.n: Postmortem CT scans of 597 paediatric decedents (6 months to 20.9 years) in New Mexico, 2011-2023, linked to county-level AQI and temperature during the 9 months before birth. Lower BMD was associated with poorer AQI in trimesters 2 and 3, trimester 2 being the candidate sensitive window; AQI was unrelated to porous cranial lesions and temperature extremes to either outcome. No effect sizes in the abstract. AQI is a composite dominated by whichever pollutant is worst on a day, assigned at county level, and a decedent sample is not representative of living children. Relevance: indirect - county AQI is the coarsest exposure surrogate; a pollutant-specific, address-level PM2.5 estimate is the obvious next step.
